2.  24-52055  Recommendation to receive and file a report from the Acting Director of Health and
  Human Services.

  Andrea Lee, Legislative & Partnerships Manager, introduced herself and discussed
  the general responsibilities of her position. Ms. Lee discussed ways the Board
  could assist with her work.

A brief discussion ensued regarding where Health Department funding comes from,
and at what percentage.

A brief discussion ensued regarding creating an advocacy packet to help inform the
Board’s efforts.

Alison King, Acting Director, provided the following information to the Board:
  • The effects of the significant storm system that impacted Long Beach,
  including sewage spills, beach closures and cleanup efforts.
  • The 2024 Point in Time Homeless Count.
  • The opening of Youth Navigation Center.
  • Los Angeles County reached out to the Department regarding an
  encampment resolution to utilize a hotel in Council District 8 to house
  individuals from a specific encampment until permanent housing solutions
  can be identified.
  • Finalizing Round two of funding for an encampment resolution for the
  Highland Hotel in Council District 2 to house up to 60 individuals from
  downtown encampments.
  • The City will be ending the Homeless Emergency Proclamation;
  however, homeless assistance will continue to be the primary focus.
  • The City is restructuring the governing structure of homeless programming,
  moving primary oversight of homeless programming administration to the
  City Manager’s office.
  • The Council has also reached out to the City regarding the possibility of
  opening a re-entry facility in Long Beach. They are currently seeking a 5,000
  square foot facility that would meet their needs.
  • Work is beginning on the City’s Fiscal Year 2025 Budget. The City is
  currently dealing with the effects of staff equity raises on the general fund,
  and the loss of Long Beach Recovery Act funding.
  • The Community Crisis Response Team has expanded into the Downtown
  Long Beach area.
  • The Department is currently monitoring for measles in response to a
  confirmed Los Angeles case.
  • The Black Infant Health Program received expansion funding which will allow
  them to continue to assist children up to the age of five. The program
  previously only assisted children up until the age of three.
  • The City’s proposal to restructure the Civil Service Department which will go
  to ballot in June.

A motion was made by Member Lesen, seconded by Member Walton, to
approve recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

Yes:  8 Sanders, Schwerin, St Bernard, Gupta, Lesen, Tejani, Walton, Clark

3.  24-52056  Recommendation to discuss Board goals and infrastructure.

  Chair Sanders informed the Board that Mr. James Suazo, who was scheduled to
  facilitate additional strategic planning discussions, was unable to attend today’s
  meeting due to an emergency.

  Chair Sanders informed the Board that interviews for the next Director of Health
  and Human Services had been scheduled for the week of February 12th, and that
  she had been selected to sit on the interview panel. Chair Sanders requested input
  from the Board on the qualities they would like to see in the new Director.

  A motion was made by Member Lesen, seconded by , to approve
  recommendation. The motion carried by the following vote:

  Yes:  8  Sanders, Schwerin, St Bernard, Gupta, Lesen, Tejani, Walton, Clark
  No:  0  None
  Recused: 0  None
  Abstain: 0  None
  Absent: 7  Betancourt, Curtis, Girgis, McNeeley, Red Eagle, Vaias, Van
  Meeveren

PUBLIC COMMENT

There was no public comment.

ANNOUNCEMENTS

Board member Lessen announced that California State Long Beach University will be holding a Well
Conference on March 22, 2024 focusing on mental health.

Board member Gupta announced that the United Nations of Long Beach Chapter will be holding a
Women’s Leadership Summit on March 17, 2024. Board member Gupta will forward information to
the Board on this event.

ADJOURNMENT

At 9:23 a.m. the meeting was adjourned.
